questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to look after a pet rabbit at home
Why chocolate eggs are eaten at Easter in Britain
Rabbits in Britain and people's mixed views of them
The life of Beatrix Potter and her children's books
questions.why: Neil and Rob talk about rabbits' history in the UK and how they're seen as both cute and tricky.

questions.q: What is Rob's view of rabbits?
options: They are pests that damage farms
They are cute, and he likes them
They are dangerous and carry disease
He has no opinion about them at all
questions.why: He calls them 'Cute, adorable and fluffy – what's not to like?'

questions.q: How did rabbits first arrive in Britain, according to Neil?
options: They were probably brought by invaders
They swam from Europe
They have always lived there
They were brought as pets in the 1990s
questions.why: He says they were believed to be brought by invaders, maybe the Romans or Normans.

questions.q: According to Victoria Dickinson, what shows rabbits have been in Britain a long time?
options: Old paintings of rabbits in country houses
Rabbit bones found in ancient castles
Old recipes for rabbit pie from the 1500s
Over 400 places with 'warren' in their name
questions.why: She says there are over 400 villages and towns with the word 'warren' in their name.

questions.q: What allowed rabbits to spread and become wild?
options: Farmers released them to control the weeds
Fox hunting grew and removed their predators
Warmer weather allowed them to breed all year
There was more food for them in towns and cities
questions.why: She says when their predators disappeared with fox hunting, rabbits multiplied.

questions.q: Why does Victoria Dickinson call the rabbit 'paradoxical'?
options: It has opposite sides, like being wild and tame
It is very hard to catch, even for skilled hunters
It is loved in some countries but hated in others
It lives both above and below the ground
questions.why: She says it's both wild and tame, timid but also a trickster.

questions.q: Why does Rob think rabbits are the perfect symbol for Easter?
options: They are good at hiding chocolate eggs in the garden
They are born in spring, just like baby chickens
They are wild and clever, just like foxes in the woods
They're tame and loved by kids, with toys and rhymes
questions.why: He says we think of them as tame, with nursery rhymes and cuddly toys.

questions.q: What has happened to rabbit numbers in the UK in the last 20 years?
options: They have doubled
They have stayed the same
They have fallen by around 60%
They have risen by around 60%
questions.why: Neil says numbers have declined by around 60 per cent over the last 20 years.
